risk_if_not_implemented: Without Remote Management of Embedded Technologies, embedded and IoT technologies may operate with unknown, insecure or unmonitored configurations, creating exploitable footholds. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Identity Compromise / Impersonation (R-AC-5), Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity (R-AM-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Operational Technology (OT) / Industrial Control System (ICS) Attack (MT-30).

compensating_control_1.name: Remote Access
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to define, control and review organization-approved, secure remote access methods.
compensating_control_1.justification: Remote Access (NET-26) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Remote Management of Embedded Technologies (EMB-15) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
compensating_control_2.description:
Automated mechanisms exist to enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for:
(1) Remote network access; 
(2) Third-party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS); and/ or
(3) Non-console access to critical TAAS that store, transmit and/or process sensitive and/or regulated data.
compensating_control_2.justification: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) (IAC-37) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Remote Management of Embedded Technologies (EMB-15) by restricting system and data access through alternative identity and access management mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
